region.text: Saigon and its defensive perimeter, beyond which the French could not seize territory in early 1859

ledger.note: 1859: the French take Saigon, their first hold in Indochina. The infobox gives 'Capture of Saigon: 17 February 1859'; after the early-1859 attack the French could not hold ground beyond the city's perimeter. The page gives no radius; the circle is the researcher's.

ledger.note: 1862: the Treaty of Saigon cedes three provinces and Poulo Condore to France. The treaty (5 June 1862 per the infobox) 'ceded Biên Hòa, Gia Định, and Định Tường provinces along with the Poulo Condore islands' and opened the Mekong delta and three northern ports to trade. The modern provinces are the researcher's reading of the three names.

ledger.note: 1863: Cambodia becomes a French protectorate. 'On 11 August 1863, Norodom signed a treaty acknowledging a French protectorate over his kingdom.' The Kingdom of Cambodia dossier starts only in 1953, so the 1863-1953 monarchy has no dossier of its own (the post-angkor-cambodia dossier ends in August 1863). Recorded on the suzerain's side.

region.text: Châu Đốc (An Giang), Hà Tiên and Vĩnh Long, the western provinces of the Mekong delta

ledger.note: 1867: France takes the western provinces of the Mekong delta. Admiral de la Grandière forced Vietnam to cede Châu Đốc (An Giang), Hà Tiên and Vĩnh Long, 'completing French control of the southern provinces'; the page gives no month. Cliopatria shows all six provinces from 1860.
1871: the conquered provinces are organised as the colony of Cochinchina, with Admiral Dupré as first governor (page, no month); the infobox lists Saigon as capital from 1862.

region.text: Bình Thuận, ceded and annexed to Cochinchina

ledger.note: 1883: Bình Thuận is annexed to Cochinchina. 'on 25 August Harmand dictated the Treaty of Huế to the cowed Vietnamese court'; Bình Thuận was ceded and annexed to Cochinchina, and Nghệ An, Thanh Hóa and Hà Tĩnh 'were transferred to Tonkin, where they would come under direct French oversight'.

region.text: Annam and Tonkin, the protectorates of the 1883 Treaty of Huế

ledger.note: 1883: Annam and Tonkin become French protectorates. By the Treaty of Huế of 25 August 1883 the Vietnamese 'accepted a French protectorate both for Annam and Tonkin'. The Nguyễn dynasty dossier ends in June 1884, so the court of 1884-1945 has no dossier of its own. The page does not mention the Patenôtre treaty of 6 June 1884. Cliopatria shows the outline only from 1885.

region.text: Tonkin, where French and Chinese troops fought from the clash at Bac Le

ledger.note: 1884: French and Chinese troops fight in Tonkin. 'a clash between French and Chinese troops at Bac Le' on 23 June 1884 triggered the crisis that led to the Sino-French War (August 1884 to April 1885) after the Tientsin Accord of 11 May 1884 had required the Chinese armies to leave Tonkin.

region.text: Tonkin

ledger.note: 1885: China gives up Tonkin. The Tientsin treaty of 9 June 1885 'forced China to abandon its historic claim to suzerainty over Vietnam' and confirmed the French protectorate over Annam and Tonkin; the Cần Vương uprising in Annam began in July 1885 and pacification of Tonkin ran to about 1896.

1887: Cochinchina, Annam, Tonkin and Cambodia are united as French Indochina. 'French Indochina was formed on 17 October 1887 from' Annam, Tonkin, Cochinchina and the Kingdom of Cambodia (the Cochinchina page: Cochinchina 'became part of French Indochina' that day).

region.text: the Sipsong Chau Tai: the 128 Vietnamese cells Cliopatria adds to Tonkin in 1890, in 'the modern-day provinces of Điện Biên, Lai Châu, Sơn La as well as western parts of Lào Cai and Yên Bái'

ledger.note: 7 April 1889: the Sipsong Chau Tai pass to French Tonkin. Sip Song Chau Tai page: it 'became an autonomous part of the French protectorate of Tonkin, and thereby of French Indochina, in 1889'; Auguste Pavie 'signed a treaty with Đèo Văn Trị, the White Tai lord of Muang Lay' on 7 April 1889; the chiefdoms had paid tribute to 'China, Vietnam, Lan Xang/ Luang Phrabang ... and/or Siam'. Cliopatria's 1890 step (128 Vietnamese cells, about 36,000 km2) matches these provinces. Counterpart as in kingdom-of-luang-phrabang /ledger/6 (loss, April 1889). Reviewer fix 2026-10-19 (was c. 1890, counterpart nguyen-dynasty, confidence 1, 'page silent').

region.text: the disputed region east of the Mekong

ledger.note: 1893: French columns take the east bank of the Mekong from Siam. In April 1893 the Governor-General sent three columns into the disputed region; a column was 'successful in evicting the Siamese commissioner at Khammuan by 25 May'; the Paknam incident followed on 13 July and a French ultimatum on 20 July.

region.text: the east bank of the Mekong

ledger.note: 1893: the war ends with the treaty. 'The conflict led to the signature of the Franco-Siamese Treaty, on 3 October 1893.'

region.text: the east bank of the Mekong, Laos

ledger.note: 1893: Siam cedes the east bank of the Mekong, which becomes French Laos. The page: land on the east bank 'was ceded to Cambodia and Laos' and 'Siam agreed to cede Laos to France'; Chantaburi was occupied temporarily and Battambang and Siem Reap were demilitarised along with a 25 km zone on the west bank.

region.text: Laos, a French protectorate

ledger.note: 1893: Laos becomes a French protectorate (infobox 3 October 1893). The same page gives 27 March 1889 for the bill making Luang Prabang a protectorate, 1898 (text) or 19 April 1899 (infobox) for Laos's integration into the Union, and the Franco-Siamese War page gives 1896 for the protectorate under the Governor-General at Hanoi: the dates disagree. The Luang Prabang and Champasak dossiers both end in October 1893 and the Kingdom of Laos dossier starts in 1953.

region.text: Chanthaburi, held as a guarantee of the 1893 treaty

ledger.note: 1893: France occupies Chanthaburi as a guarantee. 'The French demanded as guarantees the temporary occupation of Chantaburi' (Franco-Siamese War page); the French Indochina page has 'France also occupied the western part of Chantaburi'. Mirrors rattanakosin-kingdom /ledger/25. Added by the reviewer 2026-10-19.

region.text: Guangzhouwan, added on 5 January 1900

ledger.note: 1900: Guangzhouwan is added to Indochina. Infobox: 'Guangzhouwan added: 5 January 1900'; the intro dates it 1898-1945 and the page gives no lease date. The counterpart is China, then under the Qing, which the page does not name.

region.text: the west-bank lands Cliopatria adds to Laos and Cambodia in its 1905 shape besides Trat: Sainyabuli, the western half of Champasak and Meluprey (Preah Vihear)

ledger.note: 1904: Siam cedes the west-bank lands to French Laos and Cambodia. The Laos page: 'In 1902, a treaty with Siam forced the kingdom to also surrender lands on the western side of the Mekong River. These lands now form the province of Sainyabuli and the western half of Champasak Province', and 'In 1904, the present border between Laos and Cambodia was established after Siam ceded Meluprey (Preah Vihear Province) and the Kingdom of Champasak to the French.' The cells are Cliopatria's 1905 step (69 Laos cells, 48 Cambodian); rattanakosin-kingdom /ledger/34 has the matching loss (treaty of 13 February 1904). Reviewer fix 2026-10-19: confidence 1 to 2, the page names the lands.

region.text: Trat and Koh Kong

ledger.note: 1904: Siam gives Trat and Koh Kong to French Indochina. 'In 1904, to get back Chantaburi, Siam had to give Trat and Koh Kong to French Indochina'; the Cambodia page has the Franco-Siamese Treaty of 13 February 1904.

region.text: Chanthaburi, held as a guarantee of the 1893 treaty

ledger.note: 1904: France gives Chanthaburi back. 'In 1904, to get back Chantaburi, Siam had to give Trat and Koh Kong to French Indochina' (French Indochina page); the month is the treaty of 13 February 1904 (rattanakosin-kingdom /ledger/33-34). The Franco-Siamese War page instead says 'France continued to occupy Chanthaburi and Trat up until 1907'. Added by the reviewer 2026-10-19.

region.text: Champasak, annexed on 22 November 1904

ledger.note: 1904: Champasak is annexed. Infobox 'Champasak annexed: 22 November 1904'; the text says the kingdom 'was declared dissolved on 22 November 1904'. Counterpart: the page has 'Siam ceded Meluprey (Preah Vihear Province) and the Kingdom of Champasak to the French' in 1904; the kingdom-of-champasak dossier ends in October 1893 and cannot carry the mirror, rattanakosin-kingdom /ledger/34 (February 1904 loss of 'Mluprey, Champasak and Sainyabuli') does. Reviewer fix 2026-10-19 (was kingdom-of-champasak).

region.text: Trat, which became part of Thailand again on 23 March 1907

ledger.note: 1907: Trat goes back to Siam. 'Trat became part of Thailand again on 23 March 1907.'

region.text: the provinces of Battambang, Siem Reap and Banteay Meanchey

ledger.note: 1907: Siam cedes Battambang, Siem Reap and Banteay Meanchey to Cambodia. Infobox 'Franco-Siamese Treaty of 1907: 23 March 1907'; 'From this, the French gained the provinces of Battambang and Siem Reap'; the Franco-Siamese War page names Banteay Meanchey too; the Indochina page says the retrocession was 'in April 1907'.

region.text: the block of Tonkin round Hanoi that Cliopatria gives to Japan in 1941-1945 (about 105 cells at 105.5-106.3E, 20.5-22.1N); the page names no extent

ledger.note: 1940: Japan enters northern Indochina. 'Japan entered Indochina on 22 September 1940'; Japanese officers attacked the Đồng Đăng border post and besieged Lạng Sơn, which fell four days later; Japan won three airfields and a troop ceiling of 6,000 'promptly violated'. The French administration 'had largely stayed in place, albeit as Japan's puppets'. The extent is Cliopatria's Hanoi block; the page names none.

region.text: the provinces of Cambodia and Laos ceded to Thailand in 1941

ledger.note: 1941: Thailand attacks Laos and Cambodia. On 5 January 1941 the Thai armies attacked after a reported French attack at Aranyaprathet ('The Thai army swiftly overran Laos'); the French counterattack of 16 January and the Battle of Ko Chang (17 January) did not recover the ground; a ceasefire came on 28 January.

region.text: Battambang, Sisophon, Siem Reap (excluding the town) and Preah Vihear (Pailin is part of old Battambang)

ledger.note: 1941: the Tokyo treaty cedes the Cambodian provinces to Thailand. 'Japan compelled French authorities to cede Battambang, Sisophon', Siem Reap (excluding the town) and Preah Vihear; the Franco-Thai War page dates the peace treaty, signed in Tokyo, to 9 May 1941. Pailin is included as part of old Battambang by the researcher.

region.text: Champassak and Xaignabouli Province

ledger.note: 1941: the Tokyo treaty cedes two Lao provinces to Thailand. Thailand 'compelled the French colonial government to cede Champassak and Xaignabouli Province'; the month is the Franco-Thai War page's Tokyo treaty of 9 May 1941. The page does not say which bank of the Mekong was ceded.

region.text: the provinces of Cambodia and Laos ceded to Thailand in 1941

ledger.note: 1941: the war ends in Japanese-dictated cession. The peace treaty was signed in Tokyo on 9 May 1941 after armistice papers of 31 January aboard the cruiser Natori; Thailand got 'about a quarter of the territory it had sought' and paid six million piastres.

region.text: southern Indochina: Cochinchina and Cambodia, where Japan garrisoned 8,000 troops from August 1941

ledger.note: 1941: Japan occupies southern Indochina. 'Vichy France signed the Protocol Concerning Joint Defense and Joint Military Cooperation on 29 July' (the Cochinchina page has 28 July 1941); in August the army 'entered the French protectorate of Cambodia and established a garrison that numbered 8,000 troops'.

region.text: Guangzhouwan

ledger.note: 1945: Guangzhouwan goes back to China. 'In 1945, France returned Guangzhouwan to China.' The page gives no month.

region.text: Norodom's kingdom, without Battambang and Siem Reap, which Siam held until 1907

ledger.note: 1945: Japan ends French rule in Cambodia. 'the Japanese dissolved the French colonial administration on 9 March 1945'; four days later King Sihanouk 'decreed an independent Kampuchea' (a Japanese-backed state to October 1945).

region.text: Annam and Tonkin, the protectorates of the 1883 Treaty of Huế

ledger.note: 1945: Japan ends French rule in Annam and Tonkin. 'The Japanese revoked French administrative control on 9 March'; the page mentions the 'newly proclaimed Empire of Vietnam' without a date. Bảo Đại abdicated on 25 August 1945 (First Indochina War page).

region.text: Laos

ledger.note: 1945: Luang Prabang breaks with France. The king entered the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere 'on 8 April 1945', ending the French protectorate (infobox: Japanese-backed state, 8 April 1945).

region.text: the block of Tonkin round Hanoi that Cliopatria gives to Japan in 1941-1945 (about 105 cells at 105.5-106.3E, 20.5-22.1N); the page names no extent

ledger.note: 1945: Japan surrenders. 'The Japanese surrendered on 15 August 1945'; the Viet Minh began its uprising on 19 August.

region.text: southern Indochina: Cochinchina and Cambodia, where Japan garrisoned 8,000 troops from August 1941

ledger.note: 1945: the Japanese leave southern Indochina with the surrender of 15 August 1945; British forces took the south and Chinese forces the north up to the 16th parallel in September (First Indochina War page).

region.text: Vietnam, for which the DRV claimed power in September 1945

ledger.note: 1945: the Democratic Republic of Vietnam is proclaimed. 'On V-J Day (2 September 1945), Ho Chi Minh proclaimed the establishment of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam (DRV)', after Bảo Đại's abdication on 25 August. The DRV held the whole of Vietnam only for days in the south; Chinese forces occupied the north to the 16th parallel.

region.text: Vietnam south of the 16th parallel

ledger.note: 1945: the French retake the south. On 23 September 1945 the French 'declared French authority restored south of the 16th parallel' after overthrowing the DRV government in Saigon; General Leclerc arrived in October.

region.text: Norodom's kingdom, without Battambang and Siem Reap, which Siam held until 1907

ledger.note: 1945: the French protectorate of Cambodia is re-established. Infobox 'Reestablished: 16 October 1945'.

region.text: Vietnam north of the 16th parallel (Chinese occupation zone, September 1945)

ledger.note: 1946: the French return to the north on terms. In March 1946 French troops began returning under the Ho-Sainteny agreement, which 'recognized the DRV as a free state within an Indochinese Federation in the French Union'; the Franco-Chinese arrangement of February 1946 had the Chinese leave the north.

region.text: Laos

ledger.note: April 1946: the French return to Laos. Infobox 'French restoration: 24 April 1946'; the French were 'entering the capital of Vientiane towards the end of April 1946'. Laos was an Associated State in July 1949 (infobox 19 July 1949). Reviewer fix 2026-10-19 (was November 1946 at confidence 1, 'page silent').

region.text: the provinces of Cambodia and Laos ceded to Thailand in 1941

ledger.note: 1946: Thailand returns the 1941 provinces. 'The provinces annexed by Thailand in 1941 were returned to their respective nations in November.' The Cambodia page says Battambang and Siem Reap were 'recovered from Thailand after World War II'.

region.text: Vietnam north of the 16th parallel (Chinese occupation zone, September 1945)

ledger.note: 1946: the Ho-Sainteny arrangement breaks down. On 19 December 1946 hostilities between the Viet Minh and the French broke out in Hanoi and the Viet Minh government withdrew to the countryside; the Haiphong bombardment of 23 November 1946 preceded it.

region.text: northern Tonkin, the Việt Bắc where Ho Chi Minh and Giap retreated in 1947

ledger.note: 1946: the First Indochina War begins. 'Hostilities between the Việt Minh and the French broke out in Hanoi' on 19 December 1946; the Viet Minh held most of northern Tonkin after the French abandoned Lạng Sơn in October 1950. The page names no zone boundary; Tonkin is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Cochinchina, Annam and Tonkin, merged into the State of Vietnam

ledger.note: 1949: the State of Vietnam is formed within the French Union. 'Cochinchina, Annam and Tonkin were merged into the State of Vietnam within the French Union, with Bảo Đại as head of state' (June 1949; the Cochinchina page has the merger taking effect on 4 June 1949, after the Élysée Accords of March 1949). No dossier exists yet for the State of Vietnam.

region.text: Laos

ledger.note: 1953: Laos becomes independent. Infobox 'Independence: 22 October 1953'.

region.text: Norodom's kingdom, without Battambang and Siem Reap, which Siam held until 1907

ledger.note: 1953: Cambodia becomes independent. 'independence day was celebrated on 9 November 1953'; Cambodia had been an Associated State from 8 November 1949.

region.text: Vietnam

ledger.note: 1954: the State of Vietnam gains full independence. 'June 1954: The State of Vietnam gained full independence legally, though the transfer of power was incomplete.'

region.text: northern Tonkin

ledger.note: 1954: the war ends at Geneva. The Geneva Accords of 21 July 1954 gave a ceasefire and 'the division of Vietnam at the 17th parallel north'; the final ceasefire took effect on 11 August 1954 after Dien Bien Phu fell on 7 May.

region.text: all of the French Indochina of 1953, Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos

ledger.note: 1954: French Indochina ends. 'The federation lasted until 21 July 1954', the date of the Geneva Accords; Vietnam divides at the 17th parallel and Cambodia and Laos are independent.

wars.name: Cochinchina campaign

zones.text: Saigon and its defensive perimeter, beyond which the French could not seize territory in early 1859

Biên Hòa, Gia Định and Định Tường provinces, read as the modern provinces of Hồ Chí Minh City, Bà Rịa-Vũng Tàu, Bình Dương, Tây Ninh, Long An, Tiền Giang, Bình Phước and Đồng Nai inside Cliopatria's 1860 outline (the page gives no boundary)

wars.outcome: The French took Saigon on 17 February 1859 but held only its perimeter; the Treaty of Saigon (5 June 1862) ceded Biên Hòa, Gia Định, Định Tường and Poulo Condore.
wars.note: The page does not name the war; 'Cochinchina campaign' is its usual title. Saigon is recorded as occupation, the cession as gain.

wars.name: Sino-French War
wars.outcome: The Tientsin treaty of 9 June 1885 'forced China to abandon its historic claim to suzerainty over Vietnam' and confirmed the French protectorate over Annam and Tonkin.
wars.note: August 1884 to April 1885 per the page; the clash at Bac Le was on 23 June 1884.

wars.name: Franco-Siamese War

zones.text: the east bank of the Mekong

wars.outcome: Siam ceded the east bank of the Mekong by the Franco-Siamese Treaty of 3 October 1893; Chantaburi was occupied temporarily and Battambang and Siem Reap demilitarised.
wars.note: The page's infobox dates the conflict 13 July to 3 October 1893; the French columns moved from April 1893 and evicted the Siamese commissioner at Khammuan by 25 May.

wars.name: Japanese invasion of French Indochina

zones.text: the block of Tonkin round Hanoi that Cliopatria gives to Japan in 1941-1945 (about 105 cells at 105.5-106.3E, 20.5-22.1N); the page names no extent

wars.outcome: Japan entered on 22 September 1940, took the Đồng Đăng post and besieged Lạng Sơn, which surrendered four days later; the Vichy administration stayed in place under Japanese garrison.
wars.note: The extent of the occupied zone is not on the page.

wars.name: Franco-Thai War

zones.text: the provinces of Cambodia and Laos ceded to Thailand in 1941

wars.outcome: Thai armies overran Laos and western Cambodia from 5 January 1941; the ceasefire was 28 January and the Tokyo peace treaty of 9 May 1941 forced the French to give up the border provinces to Thailand; they were returned in November 1946.
wars.note: The Indochina page dates the war 'Oct. 1940 - May 1941'.

wars.name: First Indochina War

zones.text: northern Tonkin, held by the Viet Minh after October 1950

wars.outcome: Hostilities began on 19 December 1946 and ended with the fall of Dien Bien Phu on 7 May 1954 and the Geneva Accords of 21 July 1954, which divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel.
wars.note: The page names no zone boundaries; Tonkin is the researcher's reading.

certainty.note: Cochinchina's provinces and Cambodia's protectorate are named without boundaries on the pages; Tonkin was not pacified (the page: about ten further years from 1886).

Treaty frontiers: the Sino-Vietnamese border was demarcated in 1887, the Mekong frontier by the treaties of 1893, 1904 and 1907 and the Laos-Burma border by the treaty with Britain in 1896; the interior of Laos and the Annamite highlands stay approximate.
The Thai-held provinces of 1941-1946, the Japanese occupation, the Chinese and British zones of 1945-46 and the Viet Minh zones of 1946-1954 are approximate.

notes: Page budget 9, all used (French Indochina, French Cochinchina, French protectorate of Cambodia, Franco-Siamese War, Tonkin campaign, French protectorate of Laos, Franco-Thai War, First Indochina War, Japanese occupation of Vietnam). (1) Scope: the dossier follows the Cliopatria row from the capture of Saigon (17 February 1859) to the Geneva Accords (21 July 1954), as one colonial state whose name changes in 1871 and 1887; Cliopatria's row 1860..1957 is therefore corrected at both ends (its 1956-1957 shape holds no Indochina). (2) Every Cliopatria shape holds 72 to 106 cells of French possessions that are not Indochina: Réunion (55E 21S), the French settlements in India (Mahe, Karaikal, Yanam, Chandernagore), the Tianjin concession (117E 39N), New Caledonia and, from 1895, Kerguelen. The corrections cut them with a country intersection; the French colonial dossiers should take them. (3) Cliopatria draws all six Cochinchina provinces from 1860 and the Cambodian protectorate from 1868; the pages date the three eastern provinces to 5 June 1862, the western three to 1867 and Cambodia to 11 August 1863. (4) Cliopatria's 1941-1945 hole of 105 cells round Hanoi is given to its Empire of Japan shape; the pages have the French administration remaining under Japanese garrison, so the block is recorded as an occupation (ledger, confidence 2 for the event, the extent being Cliopatria's); Cliopatria's Thai shape does not show the 1941 cession either. (5) The protectorate vassalages are recorded on the suzerain's side with the continuing monarchies as counterparts (kingdom-of-cambodia, kingdom-of-laos, nguyen-dynasty); those dossiers start in 1953, 1953 and end in 1884 respectively, leaving the protectorate periods 1863-1953, 1893-1953 and 1884-1945 without a dossier. (6) Disagreements inside the pages: Laos protectorate 27 March 1889 (text), 3 October 1893 (infobox) or 1896 (Franco-Siamese War page); Laos joins the Union in 1898 (text) or 19 April 1899 (infobox); Japanese southern occupation 28 July (Cochinchina page) against 29 July 1941 (Japanese occupation page); Franco-Thai War 'Oct 1940 - May 1941' (Indochina infobox) against 'Oct 1940 - Jan 1941' (Cambodia infobox). (7) Not settled: the extent of the Japanese zones; which bank of the Mekong Champasak and Xaignabouli cover; the 1890 and 1904 steps of Cliopatria (confidence 1); the Patenôtre treaty of 6 June 1884 (not on the Tonkin page); Guangzhouwan's lease date (the page gives only the addition on 5 January 1900) and its area; the Chinese occupation of the north in 1945-46 beyond the 16th parallel; the Viet Minh zones as boundaries. (8) Counterparts needing dossiers: state-of-vietnam (1949-1955), the three protectorate monarchies above, the Empire of Vietnam, the Kingdom of Kampuchea and the Lao state of 1945 (short-lived Japanese-backed states), qing-dynasty and republic-of-china were not yet in the folder. (9) Gazetteer names needed: Guangzhouwan (place), Côn Đảo (Poulo Condore), Việt Bắc (region), Sisophon (place); Cochinchina, Annam and Tonkin exist as regions; 'Đông Nam Bộ' is the Natural Earth name that carries Đồng Nai. (10) Rulers are omitted: the page gives only the first and last governors-general.
